                            About Bangalore

                            Bangalore remains a top choice among investors, homebuyers, and working professionals seeking independent houses due to its favorable climate and thriving IT sector. The IT/ITS industry in Bangalore attracts approximately 50,000 professionals annually, and drives a steady 8–10% annual increase in housing demand.

                            Around 70% of new home buyers prefer independent houses in Bangalore over flats due to benefits like privacy, customization potential, and larger living spaces.

                            Investment in under-construction inde...Read morependent houses is also projected to yield returns of 20–25%. This growth is supported by the development of 15 new Special Economic Zones and 10 industrial parks planned to launch by 2030. Rental yields in popular areas of Bangalore, such as KR Puram and Ramamurthy Nagar average 3.5 to 4.5%, sustained by consistent demand from IT sector working professionals.

                            However, the metro expansions have been key growth drivers in the popular localities of Bangalore. Whitefield ( the most popular locality of Bangalore) saw a rise of approximately 15% in property prices after the 2023 metro extension. The 43.5 km Purple Line metro has notably cut commute times toWhitefield by up to 25 minutes. This infrastructure development has boosted demand and property prices in the area.

                            The upcoming Phase 3 metro rail project, which is expected to be completed by 2026–27, will surely enhance connectivity to key corridors, such as Sarjapur Road. The land prices in Sarjapur Road are currently averaging around ₹10,000 to ₹11,000 per square foot, with an 8–12% annual growth.

                            Devanahalli, another popular area of Bangalore located just 12 km from Kempegowda International Airport, has also witnessed significant growth. The land prices in Devanahalli rise about 15–19% yearly to an average of ₹8,500 per square foot in 2025. The growth is fueled by new business parks and expanding IT infrastructure in the locality.

                            Compared to Mumbai and Delhi, the Bangalore real estate market remains competitive. Architecturally, Bangalore’s independent homes range from colonial styles to modern smart homes, with an estimated 60% incorporating smart features by 2025. Security features such as CCTV surveillance (found in 70% of properties) and gated communities are also common in the city.

                            The real estate experts forecast a steady annual appreciation rate of 10–12% over the next five years for independent houses in Bangalore, driven by continued population growth, infrastructure expansion, and the thriving IT sector.

                            Stamp Duty and Registration Charges in Bangalore 2026

                            In Bangalore, the stamp duty rates for buying independent houses and apartments generally follow the same slab system based on property value, but the calculation base differs slightly due to how areas are measured. For independent houses, stamp duty is calculated on the total constructed area or the plot area multiplied by the guideline value, while for apartments, it is based on the super built-up area.

                            Category

                            Registration Charges for Buying a House in Bangalore

                            Stamp Duty for buying a House in Bangalore


                            Male

                            1% of the value of the house

                            5% on houses over and above INR 45 lakh

                            3 % on houses between INR 21-45 lakh

                            2 % on houses less than INR 20 lakh


                            Female

                            1% of the value of the house

                            5 % on houses over and above INR 45 lakh

                            3 % on houses between INR 21-45 lakh

                            2 % on houses less than INR 20 lakh



                            Male + Female


                            1 % of the value of the house

                            5 % on houses over and above INR 45 lakh

                            3 % on houses between INR 21-45 lakh

                            2 % on houses less than INR 20 lakh
                            Moreover, the Karnataka government levies a surcharge of 2 % and a cess of 10 % on stamp duty.

                            Bangalore Real Estate Market

                            Explore the Bangalore real estate market for houses and find out how this sector performs. Here is a detailed account of residential ready-to-move-in and under-construction houses for sale in Bangalore.

                            The real estate market in Bangalore saw a 1.9 % fall in quarterly demand. Meanwhile, supply has surged by 7.0%, contributing to a 0.8% increase in property prices.

                            Whether you’re looking for a ready-to-move-in home or considering an under-construction property in Bangalore, there is something for everyone. The under-construction segment recorded a QoQ price fall of 0.2%, and ready-to-move-in properties recorded a QoQ price growth of 1.8%.

                            3 BHK houses in Bangalore remain a top choice among buyers, accounting for 48% of the demand share. Regarding supply, 3 BHK houses account for 51% of the available properties. 2 BHK independent houses follow in Bangalore, constituting 37% of the demand share and 27%...Read more of the supply share.

                            Between Q1 2025 and Q1 2026 (Jan-Mar), residential property prices rose from Rs 11,529 per sqft to Rs 12,899 per sqft, a 43% increase, reflecting the city's resilience and long-term investment potential.

                            However, units sized between 1,250 and 2,000 per sq ft attracted the most attention, accounting for 43% of the demand, while the supply recorded a 45% market share. Southern and eastern micro-markets of Bangalore have been in high demand among homebuyers for the past few years. This demand is due to the improved accessibility to major job hubs and upgraded social and commercial amenities in these regions. Buyers preferred buying homes in Whitefield, Sarjapur Road, and Bellary Road in Bangalore.

                            Key developers that share the top active listings include Prestige Estates Projects Ltd., Brigade Enterprises Ltd., SOBHA Limited, Godrej Properties, Sattva, Puravankara Ltd., Assetz Property Group, Nambiar Builders Pvt. Ltd., Provident Housing Ltd., and Abhee Ventures Pvt. Ltd.

                            In January 2026, the Sumadhura Group scheduled plans to launch 6 large residential projects worth 8 million sq ft across East & North Bengaluru in FY26, targeting premium housing demand.
